title: Graph Triple Attention Networks: A Decoupled Perspective

problem.claim: Graph Transformers face interpretability and flexible-use issues from coupled multi-view information, plus overfitting and over-globalizing issues from coupled local message passing and global attention.

gap.claim: Existing Graph Transformer designs do not decouple positional, structural, and attribute views from local and global interactions.

contributions.claim: A decoupled perspective of Graph Transformers separates positional, structural, and attribute attention from local and global interaction levels.
DeGTA separately computes multi-view attentions and adaptively integrates multi-view local and global information.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report state-of-the-art performance across various datasets and tasks, including node classification and graph classification.
The authors report that ablation studies show decoupling improves performance and interpretability.

narrative_sequence.summary: Graph Transformers capture long-range dependencies and graph inductive biases.
Coupling multi-view information and local-global interactions creates interpretability, flexibility, overfitting, and over-globalizing challenges.
The paper introduces a decoupled perspective and implements it as DeGTA with separate multi-view attention and adaptive local-global integration.
The authors report improved interpretability, flexible design, adaptive integration, state-of-the-art performance, and supportive ablation findings.
The authors provide a code repository.

unknowns: Dataset identities, dataset sizes, and task-specific results are not reported.
No quantitative performance values or baseline comparisons are provided.
The abstract does not describe the architecture, training procedure, or ablation configurations.
